image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Six-storey modern Thai low-rise condominium, white rendered box with tall vertical grey fin panels between floor-to-ceiling tinted windows, recessed balconies with frosted glass balustrades staggered in a checkerboard pattern, a double-height ground-floor lobby with a projecting flat entrance canopy on slim steel posts, a landscaped planter strip along the base, a roof deck with a slatted timber screen hiding air-conditioning plant, and a small illuminated project name sign beside the entrance Materials: clean white render, matte dark-grey aluminium composite fins, tinted grey low-iron glass, frosted glass balustrades, light timber-look aluminium slats on the roof screen, brushed stainless canopy posts.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Low-Rise Condominium
nameTh: คอนโดโลว์ไรส์
notes: The developer-built 'low-rise condo' of the last fifteen years, the third of four six-storey residential shells and the designed, clean-lined one. Sizing: six floors at 3.2 m plus a 1.2 m roof-deck screen and a taller 3.6 m lobby floor gives 21 m; six 4 m bays give 24 m and a double-loaded corridor with 7 m deep units gives 16 m. Exterior shell only, no interior geometry: the full-height glazing and the double-height lobby are tinted near-opaque panes (opacity about 0.92, low roughness) so they read as glass rather than holes, and the roof deck is a flat slab behind a screen, not a usable level. The checkerboard balcony stagger is what distinguishes it from the cream rental block and means the balcony module is instanced at alternating bays rather than every bay. Tinted grey glass and the dark fins are exactly the band the turntable backdrop's luma of 58 sits in, so both must be authored lifted and the white render must dominate the silhouette; the render is deliberately white to keep the mean luma high. SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-27 before the build: the Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.036 : 1 : 0.842, so at the declared h = 21.0 the bounding box is 21.8 x 21.0 x 17.7; its body reads 20.5 m wide (965 px at 47.06 px/m on the +Z depth map) by 14.0 m deep with the side louvre boxes 0.65 m proud on each flank (21.8) and the entrance canopy and planter 2.2 m in front (16.55 built). The list-time 24 x 16 was a six-bay-at-4 m estimate; the proxy and plate agree on six bays of 2.5 m between 0.3 m fins, two 1.85 m louvre boxes and 0.45 m corner fins. Levels from the proxy: ground 3.05 m, five floors at 2.85 m (slab lines at 3.26 / 6.13 / 8.89 / 11.76 / 14.63 / 17.49 m), roof slab 17.75, parapet coping to 18.5, timber screen 17.75..21.0 on the REAR 40 percent of the roof (front run 7.7 m behind the facade). FACADE GRAMMAR CORRECTED from the plate: it is NOT a checkerboard -- bays A, D and F carry grid windows on every floor and bays B, C and E carry a glass-balustrade balcony on every floor, so the balcony module is instanced per bay column, not per alternating bay. Built bounding box 21.84 x 21.0 x 17.32: z from -7.72 (rear louvre slats, mirrored from the front) to +9.6 (entrance paving under a 2.5 m canopy), so d is declared 17.3.
